correctness.rationale: Every stable fixed point corresponds to a formal-concept extent by antitone Galois duality. Partition by extent/intent size: minimum side at most one contributes \(O(n)\); both sides at least three contribute \(O_c(n^{3/2})\) in expectation via rectangle first moments and geometric ratios. For one side of size two, Poisson pair-codegrees and \(O_c(n^{3/2})\) maximality losses give twice \(\Pr(\operatorname{Poi}(c^2)\geq3)/2\). The exact maximal two-by-two mean is \(\binom n2^2p^4(1-p^2)^{2(n-2)}\), while a rooted \(K_{2,2}\)/\(K_{3,2}\) Efron--Stein overlap argument bounds its variance by \(O_c(n^3)\). Together these give \(\mathbb E|S_n/n^2-F(c)|=O_c(n^{-1/2})\). The separately implemented finite verifier exhausts all binary contexts through size four; it is not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The invariant counts semantic fixed-point propositions of the two-sorted Galois closure, or equivalently the number of formal concepts. At the natural collision crossover \(p\asymp n^{-1/2}\), common neighborhoods of object pairs have nondegenerate Poisson limits, and both maximal \(2\)-by-\(2\) blocks and asymmetric rectangle classes contribute on the \(n^2\) scale. The explicit limit and quantitative concentration are a motivated asymptotic benchmark and structural classification, not a fixed-size census.
